You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-005","because":"Multiple chillers (redundant cooling systems) failed simultaneously, and the standby switchover did not take effect, so the site cannot assume remaining cooling capacity is sufficient.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S6","ALI-HKG-2022:S7"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"Mechanical cooling is down and temperatures are rising across multiple server rooms, so the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer and the buffer must be treated as finite.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S3","ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S7"]},{"rule_id":"R-006","because":"Temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient, so progressive thermal load reduction should be used before full shutdown.","signals":["ALI-HKG-2022:S3","ALI-HKG-2022:S5","ALI-HKG-2022:S7"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature; if not, plan to power down servers to prevent an even longer outage or damage to machines.","rule_id":"R-005"},{"action":"Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect automated device shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space, considering termination of non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs; if insufficient, power down servers.","rule_id":"R-006"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"incident commander","reason":"Simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems with rising temperatures and risk of exceeding safe operating thresholds."},"not_covered":["Chiller manufacturer involvement and manual isolation/restoration of individual chillers are not addressed by any rule in the pill."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Issue analysis: Air entered the cooling system of the data center due to lack of water, which affected the water circulation of the four active chillers."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"However, the four standby chillers used the same water circulation system as the four active chillers, so the failover failed."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"After recirculating the water and discharging gas, chillers could not be restarted individually because all chillers of the data center were bound into a cluster."},{"id":"F4","kind":"response","text":"At 10:30, we began to reduce loads on the computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters of the entire data center to prevent the temperature from rising too fast and causing a fire."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 15:20, the chiller manufacturer's engineers manually adjusted system configurations to unbind the chillers from the cluster and individually restart each chiller."},{"id":"F6","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"This triggered the fire sprinkler system, and water got into multiple power supply cabinets and server racks, damaging hardware and complicating the equipment restoration process."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We will also ensure that automatic failover and manual failover are both effective to avoid disaster recovery failures due to deadlocks."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"The contingency plan will include standardized emergency response processes and clarify when servers must be shut down and server rooms must be powered off."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"We will expand the scope of metrics we monitor to obtain more fine-grained data and to ensure more efficient troubleshooting."}]}
